title: Giving a Position a Body
description: The screen shows a separate illustrative marker, which we choose to give a visible body. Two complete short examples lead to focused excerpts; full_code preserves the cumulative Node3D scripts. PLAY advances the presentation without executing code. Neither the examples nor their visibility changes reveal the invisible point in the case.
concept_layer: position and representation; visibility; local and world coordinates
domain_deferred: rotation and scale of reference frames

capture_leaks.duration: Point_Trace — a current position alone does not preserve the route taken to reach it.
capture_leaks.relation: Point_Lines — another position lets us construct a displacement and a connecting line.
capture_leaks.appearance: A mesh and its material determine a marker's surface; a position value does not.
capture_leaks.frame: The same location can have different coordinates relative to different frames.

limit: A position alone does not specify a surface, a history or an interaction. These examples construct a separate visible marker and a report of its position. The invisible point in the case has no visible body to reveal.

stages.title: A position as data
stages.thinking: These values specify a position without drawing a surface. This screen follows a separate marker we could build from such data. Its scripts are displayed, not executed. The invisible point in the case remains without a body.

stages.title: Something to find
stages.thinking: Our separate example adds a sphere at the address. Its radius supplies a surface; its position locates the centre. Changing the radius would change what you could see without moving that centre. Geometry has begun to offer more than a location.
stages.code:
extends Node3D

var point_position := Vector3(1.0, 0.5, 0.0)

var marker: MeshInstance3D

func _ready() -> void:
	marker = MeshInstance3D.new()
	var sphere := SphereMesh.new()
	sphere.radius = 0.04
	sphere.height = 0.08
	marker.mesh = sphere
	marker.position = point_position
	add_child(marker)

stages.title: A colour and an address
stages.thinking: These excerpts add colour and a LOCAL label. The stored position is unchanged by either. Two decimal places make the address easier to read, while some smaller differences disappear from the report. What would you choose to show?
stages.code:

material.albedo_color = Color(0.0, 0.8, 1.0)
marker.material_override = material

stages.full_code:
extends Node3D

var point_position := Vector3(1.0, 0.5, 0.0)

var marker: MeshInstance3D
var label: Label3D

func _ready() -> void:
	marker = MeshInstance3D.new()
	var sphere := SphereMesh.new()
	sphere.radius = 0.04
	sphere.height = 0.08
	marker.mesh = sphere
	marker.position = point_position
	add_child(marker)

	var material := StandardMaterial3D.new()
	material.albedo_color = Color(0.0, 0.8, 1.0)
	material.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
	marker.material_override = material

	label = Label3D.new()
	label.billboard = BaseMaterial3D.BILLBOARD_ENABLED
	label.position = Vector3(0.0, 0.12, 0.0)
	marker.add_child(label)
	_update_label()

func _update_label() -> void:
	var local_p := marker.position
	label.text = "LOCAL (%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)" % [
		local_p.x, local_p.y, local_p.z
	]

stages.title: Hide the surface
stages.thinking: Here the separate marker would alternate visibility every two seconds, using elapsed time accumulated from delta. Its position stays fixed. The screen does not run the code; the invisible point in the case is never drawn.
stages.code:
# Excerpt; marker setup is omitted.
var elapsed := 0.0

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
    elapsed += delta
    marker.visible = (
        int(elapsed / 2.0) % 2 == 0
    )

stages.title: Whose zero?
stages.thinking: With no other transformed parent, shifting this node two units along X gives the same centre two addresses: LOCAL (1.00, 0.50, 0.00), WORLD (3.00, 0.50, 0.00). Which zero do the numbers answer to?
stages.code:
# Excerpts; marker is this node's child.
# In _ready(), shift the parent:
position = Vector3(2.0, 0.0, 0.0)

# In _update_label(), read both frames:
var local_p := marker.position
var world_p := marker.global_position

# With no other transformed parent:
# LOCAL (1.00, 0.50, 0.00)
# WORLD (3.00, 0.50, 0.00)
stages.full_code:
extends Node3D

var point_position := Vector3(1.0, 0.5, 0.0)

var marker: MeshInstance3D
var label: Label3D
var elapsed := 0.0

func _ready() -> void:
	position = Vector3(2.0, 0.0, 0.0)
	marker = MeshInstance3D.new()
	var sphere := SphereMesh.new()
	sphere.radius = 0.04
	sphere.height = 0.08
	marker.mesh = sphere
	marker.position = point_position
	add_child(marker)

	var material := StandardMaterial3D.new()
	material.albedo_color = Color(0.0, 0.8, 1.0)
	material.shading_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SHADING_MODE_UNSHADED
	marker.material_override = material

	label = Label3D.new()
	label.billboard = BaseMaterial3D.BILLBOARD_ENABLED
	label.position = Vector3(0.0, 0.12, 0.0)
	marker.add_child(label)
	_update_label()

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	elapsed += delta
	marker.visible = int(elapsed / 2.0) % 2 == 0

func _update_label() -> void:
	var local_p := marker.position
	var world_p := marker.global_position
	label.text = "LOCAL (%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)" % [
		local_p.x, local_p.y, local_p.z
	]
	label.text += "\nWORLD (%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)" % [
		world_p.x, world_p.y, world_p.z
	]
